title: Every lab must show editable CSS and the actual rendered result
learningObjectives: Explain every lab must show editable css and the actual rendered result and specify the acceptance requirements for an interactive CSS lab.

understand.concept: A learning lab must connect editable CSS declarations to a real rendered preview. Learners should be able to change values, observe the browser result, reset the example, and inspect the generated CSS. A screenshot alone is not an interactive lab.
understand.whyItMatters: A trustworthy lab teaches cause and effect. Keep learner code isolated, validate inputs, show useful errors, and make controls accessible. Do not claim a preview is real if it is only a static illustration.
understand.analogy: A lab is a working instrument: the learner changes a control and sees the actual result, not a picture of a result.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy describes the learning workflow; the real lab must use a working preview, safe state handling, and accessible interaction.

explain.narrative: This starter changes the rendered card and CSS readout together. A production lab should run in an isolated preview context and support reset and error feedback.

practise.guidedTask: Create a lab shell that accepts CSS controls, updates an isolated live preview, displays generated declarations, supports reset, and reports invalid input safely.
practise.independentTask: Implement the lab with a live isolated preview, editable controls, generated CSS, reset behaviour, and helpful error states. Test keyboard and mobile operation.
hints: Do not substitute static artwork for a real rendered preview.
Keep learner code isolated from the parent app and its secrets.
Use one source of state for controls, preview, and generated CSS.

options: Editable controls update the actual rendered preview and CSS output
questions.answer: Editable controls update the actual rendered preview and CSS output
questions.explanation: The learner must be able to change the input and observe the actual rendered result.

questions.explanation: Labs must be safe, operable, testable, and connected to actual rendered behaviour.
